intro: Base64 to File decodes a Base64 string or a data URI back into a downloadable file. Paste a full data URI (such as data:image/png;base64,...) and the tool reads the embedded MIME type, or paste a bare Base64 string and it decodes the raw bytes for you. It is handy whenever you need to turn an encoded blob from code, JSON, or a CSS asset back into the original file.
useCases: Recover an image saved as a data URI in HTML, CSS, or a JSON payload
Decode a Base64 attachment copied out of an email or API response into a real file
Inspect or download an embedded asset pulled from logs or a config file
Convert a Base64 string returned by a backend into a file to verify its contents
Extract a small PDF or font that was inlined as a data URI

faq.q: Is my data sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The decoding runs entirely in your browser using built-in JavaScript, so the Base64 string and the resulting file never leave your device and nothing is uploaded.

faq.q: What input formats does it accept?
faq.a: It accepts a full data URI in the form data:<mime>;base64,<data>, a data URI without the ;base64 flag (URL-encoded text), or a bare Base64 string with no prefix.

faq.q: How is the file type determined?
faq.a: If you paste a data URI, the MIME type is read from the prefix. For a bare Base64 string with no MIME information, it defaults to application/octet-stream.

faq.q: Does whitespace in the Base64 string cause problems?
faq.a: No. Whitespace such as line breaks and spaces is stripped before decoding, so wrapped or pretty-printed Base64 still decodes correctly.
No. Any file type can be decoded since the tool works on raw bytes; the image category just reflects the most common use of turning a data URI back into a picture.
